segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `performance.*` can be implemented with a single `clock_gettime()` call. Includes `Date`, since real JS/Node group wall-clock timing APIs together too.

notes: Milliseconds since the program's **time origin** (process start), as a `double` (sub-millisecond precision) — the origin is captured once at process start by an `llvm.global_ctors` constructor, matching the spec's origin-relative reading ([ADR-00568](../adr/00/ADR-00568.md))

Monotonic (`CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW` on macOS, nanosecond-grained like libuv's `uv_hrtime`; `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux) — unlike `Date.now()`, not tied to wall-clock time ([ADR-01270](../adr/01/ADR-01270.md))

User-timing entries as Node v24 keeps them: `mark()` returns a `PerformanceMark` (its `detail` structured-cloned), `measure(name, start?, end?)` or `measure(name, options)` returns a `PerformanceMeasure`; a missing mark throws a `SyntaxError` `DOMException`
Written in TypeScript: `lib/node/perf_hooks.ts` ([ADR-01265](../adr/01/ADR-01265.md))

`new Date()` / `new Date(ms)` / `new Date(isoString)` (the string form parses via the same logic as `Date.parse` — see [ADR-00038](../adr/00/ADR-00038.md)) / `new Date(year, month, day?, hours?, minutes?, seconds?, ms?)` (month 0-indexed, matching `getMonth()`; omitted trailing fields default like real JS — day to 1, everything after that to 0; see [ADR-00039](../adr/00/ADR-00039.md))
`getFullYear/Month/Date/Day/Hours/Minutes/Seconds/Milliseconds` (+ the `set*` setters), `getTime`/`valueOf`, `toISOString`
The `getUTC*`/`setUTC*` accessors alias the field getters/setters — since the stored timestamp is UTC, these are Node's UTC methods ([ADR-00844](../adr/00/ADR-00844.md))

A Date is an object, as in JavaScript ([ADR-01468](../adr/01/ADR-01468.md)): `===` compares identity, a Date key in a `Map`/`Set` and `includes`/`indexOf` go by identity, and a setter changes the one Date every reference to it sees; through `any` it stays that object

Local time follows the host's time zone, as Node's does: the local getters, the component constructor, the local setters, `toString` (`GMT+0300 (Eastern European Summer Time)`), `toDateString` and `getTimezoneOffset`; `Date.UTC` and the `getUTC*`/`setUTC*` accessors are UTC. An unparseable string or a `NaN` time value is an Invalid Date: `getTime()` is `NaN`, `toString()` is `Invalid Date`, `toISOString()` throws a `RangeError` and JSON gives `null` ([ADR-01315](../adr/01/ADR-01315.md)); its getters are `NaN`, `setFullYear` starts from +0 and the other setters leave it invalid; `setTime` is TimeClip(ToNumber(t)) ([ADR-01383](../adr/01/ADR-01383.md))
caveats: On Linux and macOS `toString`'s zone name comes from a built-in table of the common zones' abbreviations; a zone outside it prints the C library's abbreviation (`GMT-0300 (-03)` where Node says `(Brasilia Standard Time)`). On Windows the zone and its name come from the system's ICU, as Node's do ([ADR-01599](../adr/01/ADR-01599.md))

notes: Milliseconds since epoch, via `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, ...)`
ISO 8601 strings, with or without milliseconds: `Z` (UTC), a `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` timezone offset (converted to UTC), or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date

The ECMAScript date-time format (a date-only form is UTC, a date-time without an offset local time) and V8's legacy forms (`toString`/`toUTCString` output, `Jul 15 2024`, `2024/07/15 10:30`); unparseable input is `NaN` ([ADR-01315](../adr/01/ADR-01315.md))
Mutate the Date in place, whatever the receiver (a variable, a field, an element, a call result), and return the new time value, matching real JS ([ADR-01468](../adr/01/ADR-01468.md))
Multi-argument setter overloads cascade into the following fields (`setFullYear(y, m, d)`, `setHours(h, m, s, ms)`, …) ([ADR-00488](../adr/00/ADR-00488.md))

The strict lane rejects arithmetic on a Date as TypeScript does (TS2362, TS2363, TS2365, and TS2365/TS2322 on a compound `date += n`): the millisecond count is `getTime()` ([ADR-01134](../adr/01/ADR-01134.md), [ADR-01468](../adr/01/ADR-01468.md))
Under `-compat=js`, a compound `date += n` / `date -= n` makes the variable a string / a number, as JavaScript does

Under `-compat=js`, `date + x` concatenates the date string and `date - x` (`*`, `/`, `%`, `**`, the relational operators) reads its millisecond count, as JavaScript does ([ADR-01310](../adr/01/ADR-01310.md))
Fixed `"Www Mon DD YYYY"` shape (e.g. `"Thu Jan 01 1970"`), matching real JS exactly except for the UTC deviation

caveats: One fixed `"M/D/YYYY"` format (the default en-US shape) in local time; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support

notes: `toTimeString` is `toString`'s time and zone (`"13:04:09 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)"`); `toJSON` is `toISOString`, `null` for Invalid Date ([ADR-01333](../adr/01/ADR-01333.md))

caveats: One fixed en-US shape (`"1:04:09 PM"`, `"1/5/2020, 1:04:09 PM"`) in local time; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support

notes: `observe({ entryTypes })` / `observe({ type, buffered })`, `disconnect()`, `takeRecords()`, `supportedEntryTypes`; entries arrive on a later turn of the loop, sorted by start time ([ADR-01265](../adr/01/ADR-01265.md))

caveats: A histogram keeps exact samples, not Node's HDR histogram (3 significant figures): a percentile of large values can differ in its last digits
notes: `RecordableHistogram` (`record`, `recordDelta`, `add`) and the event-loop-delay `IntervalHistogram` (`enable`/`disable`), with `min`/`max`/`mean`/`stddev`/`percentile(s)` and their BigInt forms ([ADR-01265](../adr/01/ADR-01265.md))
Not ported from Node's `lib/internal/perf`
